paper.title: An open-access database and analysis tool for perovskite solar cells based on the FAIR data principles
paper.file_name: 42_An open-access database and analysis tool for perovskite solar cells based on the FAIR data principles.pdf
paper.research_summary: Here we extract all the meaningful device data from peer-reviewed papers on metal-halide perovskite solar cells published so far and make them available in a database. We collect data from over 42,400 photovoltaic devices with up to 100 parameters per device. We then develop open-source and accessible procedures to analyse the data, providing examples of insights that can be gleaned from the analysis of a large dataset. The database, graphics and analysis tools are made available to the community and will continue to evolve as an open-source initiative.

tasks.task_name_raw: creation of an open-access database and analysis tool for perovskite solar cells
tasks.objective: to expand the normal research cycle by collecting all perovskite solar cell data, both past and future, in one place; to make all historical data accessible and provide means to upload new experimental data; to implement interactive graphical data visualization tools that enable simple and interactive exploration, analysis and filtering
constraints: FAIR data principles (findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable)
input_requirements: peer-reviewed papers on metal-halide perovskite solar cells
metadata, process data and performance data
output_goal: interactive web-based tools for exploration, analysis, filtering and visualization
protocols and metadata ontology for reporting device data

evidence.text: Here we extract all the meaningful device data from peer-reviewed papers on metal-halide perovskite solar cells published so far and make them available in a database. We collect data from over 42,400 photovoltaic devices with up to 100 parameters per device.

stages.stage_name_raw: manual extraction of device data from peer-reviewed papers
stages.stage_goal: to collect all perovskite solar cell data ever published in one open-access database
stage_input: over 15,000 papers found in Web of Science with search phrase 'perovskite solar' up to end of February 2020

evidence.text: We have manually gone through every paper found in the Web of Science with the search phrase ‘perovskite solar’ up to the end of February 2020 (that is, over 15,000 papers). In total, we have manually extracted data for over 42,400 devices.

stages.stage_name_raw: consistent formatting of extracted data according to protocol
stages.stage_goal: to increase the usability of the data by consistently formatting it according to instruction in supporting documentation
stage_input: original data extraction protocol containing 95 attributes
stage_output: consistently formatted device data ready for database ingestion

evidence.text: Once extracted, the data have been consistently formatted according to the instruction in the supporting documentation and is now freely available in the Perovskite Database.

stages.stage_name_raw: development of interactive web-based tools for data exploration and visualization
stages.stage_goal: to provide means for simple and interactive exploration, analysis, filtering and visualization of the data without programming knowledge
stage_output: web-based tools for filtering and visualization

evidence.text: Apart from making all historical data accessible and providing means to upload new experimental data, interactive graphical data visualization tools have been implemented that enable simple and interactive exploration, analysis and filtering (Fig. 1).

stages.stage_name_raw: development of open-source analysis procedures and fitting models
stages.stage_goal: to develop free interactive web-based tools and procedures for analysis, including bandgap fitting and statistical estimation
stage_output: analysis code (e.g., second-degree polynomial fitting for bandgap)

evidence.text: With the analysis code freely available, a fitting procedure such as that in Fig. 4c could easily be done for any compositional range where sufficient data are available and it can be updated whenever new data are made available.
In Fig. 4a, the kernel density estimation, that is, the smoothed average, of the open-circuit voltage (Voc) is given for three common HTLs.

stages.stage_name_raw: demonstration of insights via example analyses
stages.stage_goal: to validate the utility of the database and tools by providing concrete examples of insights derived from aggregated data
stage_output: validated insights on record development, tandem integration, stability and scalability
figures illustrating trends (e.g., PCE vs publication date, Voc KDE, bandgap fitting)

evidence.text: We demonstrate the capabilities of the database and the associated tools by giving a few examples of insights that can be gleaned from the analysis of this large dataset in terms of, for example, record development, tandem integration, stability and scalability.

Here we extract all the meaningful device data from peer-reviewed papers on metal-halide perovskite solar cells published so far and make them available in a database. We collect data from over 42,400 photovoltaic devices with up to 100 parameters per device.
In total, we have manually extracted data for over 42,400 devices.
Once extracted, the data have been consistently formatted according to the instruction in the supporting documentation and is now freely available in the Perovskite Database.
